text:
Recent evidence supports treating recommendation judgments as multidimensional and task-specific. ConSiDERS-The-Human (ACL 2024) recommends clear criteria, simpler annotation tasks, and checks for annotator consistency and uncertainty. A 2025–2026 recommender study found that richer metadata and longer histories improved LLM–human alignment, but item-level agreement remained moderate despite strong aggregate system-ranking agreement. Aggregate agreement therefore does not establish reliable diagnosis of individual recommendations. [ConSiDERS](https://aclanthology.org/2024.acl-long.63/), [RecSys evaluation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.23312).

An actionable synthesis is to annotate topical relatedness separately from evidence of concrete usefulness: intended function, explicit compatibility, redundant function, quantity requirements, and entertainment or mood fit. For each dimension, record supported, contradicted, or unknown, with an evidence span from permitted titles, descriptions, histories, or observed feedback. Missing compatibility details warrant unknown; shared keywords do not establish usefulness, and interaction history alone does not establish ownership, desired quantity, or mood. This is a proposed operational taxonomy, not a validated taxonomy identified by the search.

Pilot the rubric with independent annotators; report agreement per dimension, label prevalence, unknown rates, and coverage—the fraction receiving supported or contradicted judgments. Preserve disagreements and audit lexical proxies against human labels before using them diagnostically. Netflix’s 2026 recommendation-explanation work provides a relevant operational precedent: curated human labels and rationales, explicit evaluation rubrics, and continuing human review for drift. Its findings concern explanation evaluation, so transfer to product compatibility or redundancy requires separate validation. [Netflix judge lifecycle](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18300).
